memos.headline: Momentum bifurcation: S05/S07/S09 lead at highs while S02/S04 break down hard
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market as of January 30. The strongest relative-strength names—S05 (+75% over 26w, just 0.1% off its 52w high), S07 (+51.6% over 26w, -1.2% from high), and S09 (+28.1% over 26w, sitting at its 52w high with RSI 80.6)—continue to trend well above both moving averages, though S09's parabolic extension 15.4% above its 50d mean and RSI north of 80 warns of a near-term pullback risk. On the other side, S02 is in freefall: -19.5% in a single week, -52.1% drawdown from its 52w high, RSI 32.5, and trading nearly 13% below both its 50d and 200d means—this is a broken chart I want no part of until it stabilizes. S04 is similarly weak at -20.6% drawdown, RSI 32.6, and persistent negative relative strength (-18% vs SPY over 12w). I have highest conviction in the trend leaders S05 and S07 and in avoiding the wreckage in S02 and S04; the middle names (S03, S06, S08, S10) are range-bound and uninspiring.

views.note: Near 52w high with +75% 26w gain, +44% above 200d, RSI 65.7 not yet overbought; would reassess on a close below 310 (~8% pullback).
Strong uptrend +51.6% over 26w, just 1.2% off highs, +13.3% 4w relative strength vs SPY; a close below 600 would change my view.
Trend is powerful (+24.3% 12w) but RSI 80.6 and 15.4% extension above 50d mean signal exhaustion risk; would turn long on a pullback to ~130 with RSI reset.
Catastrophic breakdown: -52.1% drawdown, -19.5% in one week, RSI 32.5, 13% below both key averages—no sign of stabilization; need a base above 310 to reconsider.
Persistent downtrend with -20.6% drawdown, RSI 32.6, -18% relative strength vs SPY over 12w; would need a reclaim of the 200d mean (~486) to turn neutral.
Quietly improving: +5.9% over 4w, reclaiming 50d mean, +4.4% relative strength vs SPY; still below 200d mean so conviction is moderate—a close below 145 negates the setup.
Choppy and below 50d mean with -6.5% 4w relative strength; no edge either way until it clears 320 or breaks 290.
Mid-range consolidation 3.3% below 50d mean but still 9.6% above 200d; RSI 48 is directionless—watching 250 support and 270 resistance.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Deliver Exceptional Earnings Growth; S02 and S09 Flash Margin Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable high-margin compounders and names where earnings power is compressing. S10 stands out with 62.5% YoY revenue growth, a 56% net margin, and only $8.47B in total debt — the cleanest balance sheet and strongest operating leverage in the group. S04's just-filed Q2 shows $81.27B in revenue (+16.7% YoY) with a 47.3% net margin and net income up 59.5%, confirming sustained pricing power. On the other side, S02 posted a 61.2% YoY decline in net income on a razor-thin 2.1% net margin despite 12.2% revenue growth, signaling severe cost or mix headwinds, while S09 is the only name with negative revenue growth (−5.2%) paired with shrinking earnings (−12.3%). I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and a return to positive top-line growth in S09 before reconsidering either.

views.note: 62.5% revenue growth, 56% net margin, minimal leverage ($8.47B debt) — best earnings momentum and balance sheet quality in the universe.
Fresh Q2 filing shows 47.3% net margin and 59.5% YoY net income growth on $81.27B revenue with manageable $40.26B debt.
Solid 34.2% net margin, 15.9% revenue growth, 33% earnings growth, and low $14.79B debt make this a reliable compounder.
Revenue of $180.17B (+13.4%) and 38.2% earnings growth are encouraging, but 11.8% net margin leaves limited cushion if growth decelerates.
86.4% YoY net income jump is impressive but $90.68B in total debt and only 7.9% revenue growth suggest the earnings surge may not be repeatable.
31% net margin is healthy but $427.2B in total debt dwarfs the rest of the universe; 8.8% revenue growth is modest for that leverage profile.
Only 1.5% revenue growth and a 6.7% decline in net income; 19.4% margin is decent but trajectory is flat — need to see re-acceleration.
9.5% revenue growth is respectable but net income fell 6.7% and $31.74B debt on $17.64B quarterly revenue is heavy; margin compression is the concern.
Revenue declining 5.2% YoY with an 8.8% net margin and 12.3% earnings drop signals deteriorating competitive position; would reconsider on positive top-line inflection.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to a 2.1% margin despite 12.2% revenue growth — severe cost or mix problem that $80.14B in debt makes harder to fix.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Sticky Inflation and Rising Long Rates Favor Selectivity Over Broad Duration Bets
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime—the upper bound has fallen 75 bp over the past year to 3.75%, with 50 bp of that in the last three months alone—but the cycle is maturing. CPI is running at 2.7% y/y, still above target, and the 10y yield has actually risen 15 bp over three months to 4.26%, steepening the 10y-2y spread to +71 bp. Unemployment at 4.4% is stable over three months but up 30 bp y/y, consistent with a mild slowdown rather than recession. My regime call is 'late easing / soft-landing': supportive for banks (steeper curve, still-decent credit) and quality cyclicals, but I am cautious on pure duration-sensitive growth given the backup in long rates and on energy given the demand softness implied by rising unemployment. A CPI print accelerating above 3% y/y or unemployment jumping above 4.6% would force me to revisit this framework.

views.note: Banks benefit from a steepening curve (+37 bp y/y in 10y-2y spread) and still-healthy labor market supporting credit quality.
Quality cyclicals should hold up in a soft-landing with easing policy rates and stable unemployment, though I watch for further labor deterioration.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from the 15 bp rise in 10y yields over three months despite ongoing Fed cuts; I need long rates to stabilize before turning constructive.
Staples offer defensive value but limited upside in a soft-landing regime where risk appetite should persist; no strong macro catalyst either way.
Energy faces demand-side risk from a gradually softening labor market (unemployment +30 bp y/y) and global growth uncertainty implied by the mild slowdown regime.
Rate-sensitive sectors with shorter-duration cash flows benefit from lower front-end rates while the steeper curve signals growth expectations remain positive.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S02 and S04 Crushed While S07 and S01 Rally on Results
memos.body: I am seeing a sharp sentiment split across the universe as earnings season unfolds. S02 dropped -19.6% on its Jan-27 results filing and S04 fell -10.0% on its Jan-28 report, signaling deeply negative narrative shifts that are unlikely to be fully priced given the magnitude of the moves. On the positive side, S07 posted a +3.4% reaction to its Jan-29 earnings and S01 gained +2.6% on its Jan-22 results, both suggesting constructive tone that could carry further if broader coverage turns supportive. S08's muted +0.5% reaction to yesterday's earnings filing suggests the market is indifferent, while S06's -4.2% drop on Jan-13 results followed by continued corporate activity (director changes, other events) keeps its narrative unsettled.

views.note: Fresh +3.4% earnings reaction on Jan-29 signals positive narrative momentum that may not yet be fully reflected in positioning.
Solid +2.6% earnings reaction on Jan-22 with supportive Reg FD disclosure suggests constructive tone building.
A -19.6% post-earnings collapse on Jan-27 represents a severe negative narrative shift that likely has further downside as coverage digests the miss.
The -10.0% earnings reaction on Jan-28 is a clear negative tone break and sentiment likely remains under pressure near-term.
The -4.2% earnings drop on Jan-13 combined with ongoing director turnover and other events keeps the narrative unsettled; I lack conviction but lean cautious.
Muted +0.5% reaction to Jan-29 earnings suggests market indifference; two recent director changes add noise but no clear directional signal.
Only a director change filing on Jan-23 with no earnings data yet; insufficient signal to form a directional view.
Reg FD disclosure on Jan-7 and a Dec director change provide no strong sentiment catalyst; awaiting earnings for a clearer read.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Retreating but WTI Surge and VIX Spike Signal Emerging Geopolitical Energy Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 44% over the past month to 248.94, suggesting the acute policy shock that drove it higher has faded, yet it remains elevated in absolute terms. Meanwhile, WTI crude has jumped nearly 12% in a month to $64.77/bbl, which I read as a supply-side tightening signal—possibly sanctions enforcement or OPEC discipline—rather than demand-driven, given the still-tight HY OAS at 2.77% and a steepening yield curve (+22bp over 3 months on the 10y-2y spread). The VIX rose 19% month-over-month to 16.88, a modest but notable uptick that aligns with renewed hedging around geopolitical or trade-policy tail risks. I have limited company-specific geopolitical intelligence from the 8-K filings in hand (all Reg FD or Other Events disclosures without detail), so my conviction is moderate; a new round of export controls on semiconductors or an escalation in energy sanctions would materially change my positioning.

views.note: No company-specific filings and no clear geopolitical exposure signal; staying on the sideline until more data emerges.
Two 8-Ks in January (Reg FD and Other Events) suggest active disclosure but without content detail I cannot assess geopolitical exposure directionally.
Back-to-back Reg FD filings in January may relate to guidance updates; absent specifics on supply-chain or China exposure, I hold neutral.
Rising WTI (+12% 1m) benefits energy-linked names if the move is sanctions-driven and structural rather than transient; would reverse on a sanctions relief deal.
Early-January Reg FD filing offers no geopolitical signal; policy uncertainty decline is mildly supportive but conviction is low.
VIX uptick and still-elevated policy uncertainty index suggest hedging cost pressure on names with concentrated geopolitical supply chains; I lean cautious here.
